pr_snapshot.body:
VP8's x64 picker filters the horizontal macroblock edge and three internal edges separately. Share their twenty-row window through the existing exact byte-domain Go SIMD network, carrying updated samples in the original edge order. AVX2, threshold and full-span guards decline unsupported work before writing; the existing vertical path remains in use.

The SIMD generator emits this horizontal specialization from the canonical ARM network. Adds independent scalar, short-window/canary, disabled-backend and vertical-decline tests. Six new decoder caller benchmarks restore the exact 400-byte input window each iteration and check the complete result against the separate public edge operations. The native harness now compares 94 cases against identical assembly/main fixtures.

Correctness: native full `go test ./...` passes after correcting a missing upstream citation; purego and SIMD-off pixel/DSP/decoder suites, required-SIMD AMD64 checkptr scalar oracles, ordinary full AMD64 decoder suite, and all six fixture output checks pass. Rosetta establishes correctness only. All 14 generated SIMD files match isolated regeneration, and PGO/format/no-assembly/build-selection gates pass. PGO is refreshed; no x64 performance claim is made before this PR's native results arrive.

Also preserves the completed PR #26 native/C audit and ARM post-push evidence outside README. On M4 Max the existing fused filter is 1.85–1.86× faster than assembly when no pixels need changing, while active-filter cases remain about 10% slower. Those are existing ARM component results, independently scoped from this new x64 change and whole-codec results. Correctness-verified representative kernel wins of at least 1.5× stay even when overall performance is flat.
